image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Triceratops skull fossil (or high-fidelity replica) mounted on a metal stand in an outdoor botanical garden setting. The skull features the characteristic three horns and large frill. The background contains green foliage, palm trees, and a distant hillside.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops cranial structure with two massive supraorbital horns and a smaller nasal horn. The morphology matches the taxonomic description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject is a skeletal fossil; the keratinous beak (soft tissue) is not preserved or present in this image, only the underlying rostral bone is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image frame is cropped tightly around the head and neck; the body and limbs are completely outside the field of view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, solid parietal-squamosal frill is clearly visible extending behind the skull, matching the structural description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as a solid bony plate. While weathered/fossilized texture is present, the structural integrity matches the 'solid bone' description rather than fenestrated variants.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As a skeletal specimen, no skin, scales, or soft tissue integument is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the cropped composition.
The tail is outside the frame.
